scope: Finite-disturbance diagnostic for two generic transistor candidates; not a physical startup test, global stability proof or oscillator qualification.
finding: All tested pulses return to the pre-disturbance plateau with no late clock edges. Timestep-paired plateau agreement does not qualify the intervening transient.
nextQuestion: Review device dynamics and operating-point applicability; these disturbances provide no evidence for adopting either candidate as the oscillator model.

baseline.scope: Reference oscillator with closed BR1, fixed schematic values and ideal 10 ns supply ramp. A 100 ns current pulse at OSC_RC after 10 us probes finite-disturbance recovery. These injected stimuli are not specimen noise or a manufacturer startup test. Late edges and plateau comparisons do not qualify startup, global stability or phase convergence.
baseline.currentConvention: Positive current removes charge from OSC_RC; negative current injects charge.
